publication_year_note: Published 5 July 2022 in Land 2022, Volume 11, Article 1021 (Received: 25 May 2022; Accepted: 1 July 2022; Published: 5 July 2022).
rationale: This practice-research case study critically reviews a pilot intergovernmental urban-rural partnership (codified via a Memorandum of Agreement between Dhenkanal municipality and 17 gram panchayats) for faecal sludge management in Odisha, India. Although it references background descriptive statistics from secondary operational records and a prior 2020 household survey (e.g., 50% FSTP capacity utilization, 13% rural share of households served in 2019-2020, 67% vs 94% septic tank shares in Figure 6, and a 50% reduction in the rural distance surcharge), it performs no statistical hypothesis testing, regression analysis, or uncertainty estimation (no SEs, CIs, test statistics, or p-values anywhere in the 16-page full text). Flagging quantitative synthesis eligibility is therefore overstated.
